territorial_scope.description: Amends the federal Social Security Act and applies to the Medicare program nationally.

evidence.quote: The Secretary shall establish a pilot program to test the use of predictive risk-scoring algorithms to provide oversight of relevant transactions

summary.short: Amends Social Security Act §1128K to require the HHS Secretary to run a two-year pilot, beginning by January 1, 2026, using a predictive risk-scoring algorithm to oversee Medicare payments for durable medical equipment and clinical diagnostic laboratory tests. Participation by beneficiaries is voluntary.
summary.long: The bill, the Medicare Transaction Fraud Prevention Act, adds subsection (d) to Social Security Act §1128K. It requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to run a two-year pilot, beginning no later than January 1, 2026, that tests a predictive risk-scoring algorithm to oversee Medicare claims for durable medical equipment and clinical diagnostic laboratory tests. Only beneficiaries who opt in to electronic Medicare Summary Notices and the pilot participate, and they may withdraw at any time. The algorithm learns from beneficiary data and scores relevant transactions from 1 (least risky) to 99 (most risky), considering listed factors such as the absence of a prior provider relationship, aberrant billing patterns, electronic fund transfer changes and ownership changes. Before implementation the Secretary must require testing, evaluation and review, establish notice methods for affected beneficiaries, providers and suppliers, and set up communication with the HHS Office of Inspector General. For transactions scoring above a risk level set by the Secretary, the Secretary reviews whether to suspend the transaction; beneficiaries may seek to cure inaccurate data or confirm the transaction by email or phone. Suspended transactions trigger electronic Medicare Summary Notices, sent at two-week intervals for three months. Any suspension must be based on human review. The Secretary may also decide when Medicare cards are terminated or reissued to prevent fraud and abuse.

notes: Relations are the amendment of Social Security Act §1128K and the cross-reference to Executive Order 14179. The new subsection (d) also cites Social Security Act §1861(u), (d) and (n), which are provisions of the act already listed in the amends row. Text inconsistencies: the subsection (d) heading reads 'predictive risk-Scoring' (capital S) while the body uses lowercase; §1128K(d)(6)(B)(iii) names the 'Department of Health and Human Service' (singular). 'Relevant transaction' is defined as a claim 'as determined by the Secretary' (§1128K(d)(8)(B)), so the scope is left to the Secretary. Status: introduced bill, text as introduced.
